answer: To deter Sybil attacks, agents must burn verifiable cryptographic stake scaled superlinearly with identity count, imposing extreme economic friction. Registering n identities costs O(n²), making mass counterfeit nodes exponentially ruinous. Like anchoring a barge at an industrial wharf or carving foundations into rugged karst, sustained operational legitimacy demands tangible sacrifice rather than cheap spam, rendering zero-marginal-cost attacks as futile as trading base copper for scarce network consensus.
